orders.challenge_claim: Attributing Song.5.1's garden-report clause to 'the man' crosses the 4:16|5:1 voice seam without quoting the gender-marked formula anchor that grounds it, even though that evidence sits in the same verse the row already cites.
orders.grounds: Verified on the bytes and squarely within the moderate voice-attribution policy. The row rests the man-voice premise on בָּ֣אתִי לְגַנִּי֮ (byte, oshb:Song.5.1), a 1cs perfect that is not gender-marked and cannot by itself carry a voice attribution; the attested tier-1 anchor sits two words later in the same verse, אֲחֹתִ֣י כַלָּה֒ (byte, oshb:Song.5.1), his address vocabulary (bride-epithet form: 5 verses, word-bound, MT 4:9, 4:10, 4:12, 5:1, 5:2; kallah: 6 verses, MT 4:8-4:12 and 5:1), and is never quoted. The policy is explicit that every voice-shift seam claim quotes the gender-marked or attested-anchor Hebrew form, spliced and tier-labeled, and that continuity alone is tier-2 corroboration - so as shipped the cross-part seam is argued at tier-2 while tier-1 evidence lies unquoted inside the row's own span. LF's audit of the row against heading-leaning is correct and worth recording: the tier-4 speaker apparatus is explicitly refused and the plural-summons hedge is held open at the tier the bytes support, so the defect is a missing quotation, not a heading-lean. CONVERGENCE: this row is also challenged by OL. The two items are DISTINCT defects - LF's is the missing in-verse tier-1 anchor for the man-voice premise; OL's is the unanchored cross-part continuity assertion plus two undisclosed byte-true straddles - but they share one root, recorded here as a NEW FINDING neither primary states: the 4:16|5:1 seam is argued from its own bytes by NEITHER row. P01-019 defers the boundary forward ('that reply belongs to the verse immediately following it, argued separately on its own bytes') and P02-001 defers it backward ('closing the movement that opened before this part's own span'), so a seam that IS byte-supportable at tier-1 from both sides - her-word-for-him at oshb:Song.4.16 against his address vocabulary at oshb:Song.5.1 - currently has no tier-1 driver stated in either row. The launch note is right that this is a work-unit boundary and not a literary claim; the mutual deferral is the hazard that boundary created.
orders.remedy: Field boundary_rationale (P02-001), executed as ONE seam-pair edit with P01-019: quote the tier-1 anchor already standing in the verse - his address vocabulary at oshb:Song.5.1, spliced and tier-labeled byte, with its object named (bride-epithet form: 5 verses; kallah: 6 verses, both word-bound) - as the ground for the man's voice, instead of resting it on a 1cs perfect. State the seam positively from both sides so neither row defers it to the other. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS (the test that killed the original): the voice attribution must be carried by a quoted, spliced, tier-labeled gender-marked or attested-anchor form; a 1cs perfect carries no gender and cannot pass, and the cure must not migrate to the tier-4 speaker apparatus, which remains never-evidence in either direction.

orders.challenge_claim: The cross-part continuity the row asserts is left with no byte anchor while two byte-true chains straddle its front seam undisclosed, and the widened-address point leans on the WEB rendering of a dod-family plural the row never names. (severity as filed: low)
orders.grounds: Limbs 1 and 2 verify; limb 3 is largely conceded by OL itself and should not carry weight; severity as filed is too low, because the undisclosed straddles are a mandated disclosure that argues continuity against this row's own front seam at the cross-part boundary - hence refine. Limb 1 UPHELD: the rationale asserts that the verse closes a movement opened before the part's own span while naming no verse and quoting no form, and the front-seam neighbour appears nowhere in boundary_evidence_refs. Limb 2 UPHELD and re-derived: two byte-true chains straddle the front seam undisclosed - יָבֹ֤א דוֹדִי֙ לְגַנּ֔וֹ וְיֹאכַ֖ל (byte, oshb:Song.4.16) answered clause-for-clause by בָּ֣אתִי לְגַנִּי֮ with its eat-verb echo at אָכַ֤לְתִּי (both byte, oshb:Song.5.1), and אֲחֹתִ֣י כַלָּה֒ (byte, oshb:Song.5.1) continuing the man's address vocabulary attested at MT 4:9, 4:10 and 4:12 (bride-epithet form: 5 verses; kallah: 6 verses, word-bound). Standing law makes an undisclosed byte-true cross-seam device an argument for continuity against the row, and here it bears directly on whether Song.5.1 should be held with Song.4.16 at all. Limb 3 REFINED DOWN: the widened-address claim is in fact byte-anchored independently of any rendering by אִכְל֣וּ רֵעִ֔ים (byte, oshb:Song.5.1), which OL concedes; what genuinely remains is that the verse-final דּוֹדִֽים (byte, oshb:Song.5.1) is a dod-family plural, a different object from the 24-verse dodi-exact set of the surrounding verses and the form the closing word of “Eat, friends! Drink, yes, drink abundantly, beloved.” (web:Song.5.1) renders - unnamed where the rendering is cited. That is a naming gap, not a leaning defect. CONVERGENCE: distinct from LF's item on this row (missing in-verse tier-1 anchor), with the shared root recorded in that ruling - the 4:16|5:1 seam is argued by neither row on its own bytes. The setumah at MT 5:1 is correctly tiered single-witness and the tier-4 speaker apparatus is explicitly refused.
orders.remedy: Two edits, one row (P02-001), merged with the P02-001/LF edit as one seam-pair cure. (1) boundary_evidence_refs: add the front-seam neighbour (web:Song.4.16 and oshb:Song.4.16), which the continuity assertion argues but does not mirror. (2) device_notes: disclose both straddles - the garden-and-eat answer from oshb:Song.4.16 to oshb:Song.5.1, and the address-vocabulary chain continuing from oshb:Song.4.12 - and state why the possessor change and the addressee change still cut the seam; where the rendering's closing 'beloved' is cited, name the verse-final form as a dod-family plural, distinct from the 24-verse dodi-exact object. TESTS THE CURE MUST PASS: every verse argued in prose outside the row's own span must appear in boundary_evidence_refs; no byte-true device may straddle the row's own seam undisclosed; and the widened-address claim must rest on the spliced plural summons at oshb:Song.5.1, not on the rendering.

orders.challenge_claim: unit_type 'dialogue_exchange' is applied to an atomized single-voice question that contains no alternation, contrary to the category's own definition, and no deviation disclosure is given.
orders.grounds: Re-derived from bytes. MT 5:9 = WEB 5:9 (crosswalk-checked, outside the offset zone) is one uninterrupted chorus turn: the doubled interrogative מַה דּוֹדֵ֣ךְ מִדּ֔וֹד (oshb:Song.5.9, byte tier) occurs twice in-verse and the two runs are byte-identical (byte sweep: 1 verse book-wide, 2 occurrences in-verse), and the verse carries no second turn - the answering wasf is a separate row at web:Song.5.10-Song.5.16. In the closed vocabulary dialogue_exchange is rapid attributed alternation held as ONE unit; a single turn does not carry that form, and the operative-category law that permits any vocabulary value the row's own bytes carry also requires a one-sentence deviation disclosure, which the device note (intra-verse doubling only) does not supply. Tier-1 bounding markers do exist on both edges under the moderate voice policy - the 2fs suffix on דּוֹדֵ֣ךְ (oshb:Song.5.9, byte tier) fixing a female addressee against the 1cs voice of the preceding narrative, and her own answering opener דּוֹדִ֥י (oshb:Song.5.10, byte tier) - which is the lyric_address pattern, not the dialogue_exchange one.
orders.remedy: Re-label unit_type to lyric_address and cite the two tier-1 bounding markers as spliced, tier-labelled forms (the 2fs addressee suffix at oshb:Song.5.9; the answering opener at oshb:Song.5.10); or keep dialogue_exchange and add the mandated one-sentence deviation disclosure in device_notes. observed_substrate_signals is a dependent field and must be re-cut with whichever label survives. Cure test (the test that killed the original): a reviewer reading only the row's own span bytes must find the form the unit_type names - MT 5:9 alone must exhibit alternation if dialogue_exchange is kept. A third cure, widening the span to web:Song.5.9-Song.5.16, is a boundary PROPOSAL only (explicit boss adoption required) and collides with the web:Song.5.10-Song.5.16 wasf bound that both primaries supported.

orders.challenge_claim: The chorus attribution is built on an addressee marker only, dropping the verse's plural-speaker form and the quoted-back oath that straddles the front seam; the attribution 'lands exactly on' the tier-4 WEB voice heading; and the device note contradicts a byte-tier cross-verse recurrence.
orders.grounds: DISTINCT from the LF item on this row, not the same defect: LF challenges the unit_type, OL challenges the evidence base. Two sub-claims verified, two mis-framed. VERIFIED: הִשְׁבַּעְתָּֽנוּ (oshb:Song.5.9, byte tier) carries the 1cp object suffix and is the only in-verse form that makes the speakers plural; it is uncited, so the PLURAL chorus identification is under-evidenced. VERIFIED: the oath root straddles the row's own front seam - הִשְׁבַּ֥עְתִּי (oshb:Song.5.8, byte tier) against הִשְׁבַּעְתָּֽנוּ (oshb:Song.5.9, byte tier), skeleton sweep: 5 verses (MT 2:7, 3:5, 5:8, 5:9, 8:4), the root being oath-only in this book with the speech roles split (adjuration at 5:8; the daughters quoting it back at 5:9) - and the rationale gives a forward reason for the cut only, so the cross-seam cohesion rule is unmet. REFINED (1): that a 2fs suffix 'cannot carry a daughters-attribution' overstates the moderate policy - a 2fs addressee marker set against the 1cs voice of the preceding narrative IS a tier-1 warrant for a shift AWAY from her voice; what it cannot carry is the plural identity. And 'lands exactly on the tier-4 heading' is a provenance inference, not a byte finding: the heading catalog audits a claim AGAINST heading-leaning, it cannot establish that a row leaned on one, and tier-4 is never evidence in either direction. REFINED (2): the charge that the device note contradicts a recurrence claim is an object error - the note's disclaimer object is מַה דּוֹדֵ֣ךְ מִדּ֔וֹד (byte sweep: 1 verse book-wide, 2 in-verse, byte-identical), which is genuinely intra-verse-only. The real gap is a different object: the row quotes הַיָּפָ֖ה בַּנָּשִׁ֑ים (oshb:Song.5.9) inside its own run, and that IS a byte-tier cross-verse recurrence (byte sweep: 3 verses - MT 1:8, 5:9, 6:1), untier-labelled and undisclosed.
orders.remedy: In boundary_rationale, splice and tier-label הִשְׁבַּעְתָּֽנוּ (oshb:Song.5.9, byte tier) as the plural-speaker evidence, keeping the 2fs addressee marker as the shift-away-from-her warrant it actually is. Add a cross-seam disclosure sentence for the oath root shared with oshb:Song.5.8 (skeleton sweep: 5 verses; oath-only root, speech role named on each side), and add web:Song.5.8 to boundary_evidence_refs so the mirror holds. Tier-label the הַיָּפָ֖ה בַּנָּשִׁ֑ים vocative as a byte-tier recurrence (byte sweep: 3 verses) or drop the quoted run. Add nothing about the WEB voice heading in either direction. Cure test: every voice-IDENTITY word in the row must trace to an in-verse form that marks the SPEAKER, not the addressee, and every cross-verse recurrence sentence must name its object and its tier.

orders.challenge_claim: The daughters-attribution again rests on an addressee marker rather than the verse's plural-speaker forms; the mutual-belonging shape discipline is performed entirely in transliteration with neither rival spliced, one of them located by position instead of a coordinate inside the offset zone; and the closing-clause bond with the named rival is undisclosed and mis-weighted at tier.
orders.grounds: Three sub-claims verified, one mis-framed. VERIFIED: the cited דּוֹדֵ֔ךְ (oshb:Song.6.1, byte tier) marks only the addressee, while וּנְבַקְשֶׁ֖נּוּ (1cp) and עִמָּֽךְ (2fs) in the same verse (oshb:Song.6.1, byte tier) - the forms that actually make the speakers plural - go uncited; the same under-evidencing class as the MT 5:9 row, so this is a cluster-level pattern, not an isolated slip. VERIFIED: neither rival shape is spliced, against the engagement-class rule that pointed splices plus tier labels are mandatory for every boundary-relevant Hebrew claim; the attested rivals are דּוֹדִ֥י לִי֙ וַאֲנִ֣י ל֔וֹ (oshb:Song.2.16, byte tier) and אֲנִ֣י לְדוֹדִ֔י וְעָלַ֖י תְּשׁוּקָתֽוֹ (oshb:Song.7.11 = web:Song.7.10, byte tier). VERIFIED and tier-corrected: the row's close הָרֹעֶ֖ה בַּשׁוֹשַׁנִּֽים (oshb:Song.6.3) and the rival's close הָרֹעֶ֖ה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּֽים (oshb:Song.2.16) are identical at SKELETON tier only (skeleton sweep: 2 verses; byte sweep: 1 verse each - they split on the shin dagesh), so this is a closer cross-verse bond than the word-order contrast the note actually draws, and any byte-identity claim there would be false. REFINED on framing: OL calls the missing coordinate an offset-zone disclosure failure, but the offset-zone rule binds STRUCTURED refs and the device note writes no ref at all, so no offset-zone violation occurs there. The actual violation is the register purge - 'held later in this part' is a positional/part reference where cross-row references must be verse-anchored. Also refined: the remark that a high confidence band 'sits oddly' here is taste, not defect - the row's close does rest on a tier-1 formula anchor that survives the bytes, and the confidence band is not challenged by this ruling.
orders.remedy: Splice both rival shapes into device_notes with tier labels and verse-anchored coordinates - דּוֹדִ֥י לִי֙ וַאֲנִ֣י ל֔וֹ (oshb:Song.2.16, byte tier) and אֲנִ֣י לְדוֹדִ֔י וְעָלַ֖י תְּשׁוּקָתֽוֹ (oshb:Song.7.11 = web:Song.7.10, byte tier; the dual is mandatory there) - replacing 'held later in this part' entirely. Add the shared closing clause as a skeleton-tier bond (skeleton sweep: 2 verses; byte sweep: 1 verse each, splitting on the shin dagesh) rather than leaving the word-order contrast as the only stated relation. In boundary_rationale, cite וּנְבַקְשֶׁ֖נּוּ and עִמָּֽךְ (oshb:Song.6.1, byte tier) as the plural-speaker evidence. Cure tests: no positional or part reference survives in any field; every offset-zone coordinate written anywhere on the row carries a dual; and every recurrence sentence names its tier, with no byte-identity wording on the shin-dagesh pair.

orders.challenge_claim: LF and OL raise the SAME core defect - 'bounded on both sides by a person-form shift' fails on the front edge, since MT 6:9 and MT 6:10 are alike third-person feminine predication. OL adds two DISTINCT defects: the three-site recurrence is carried at a tier the row never names, and the 'ascending' label imports an element absent from the verse's own bytes.
orders.grounds: All three sustained on re-derivation. FRONT SEAM (same defect in both packets): the word-final-kaf audit finds zero 2fs forms in EITHER MT 6:9 or MT 6:10; MT 6:9 predicates הִיא֙ three times with the 3fs mappiq suffixes לְאִמָּ֔הּ / לְיֽוֹלַדְתָּ֑הּ (oshb:Song.6.9, byte tier), and MT 6:10 continues feminine-singular predication with הַנִּשְׁקָפָ֖ה (oshb:Song.6.10, byte tier). The last actual 2fs address in the neighbourhood is לְצַמָּתֵֽךְ (oshb:Song.6.7, byte tier), three verses earlier; the יוֹנָתִ֣י תַמָּתִ֔י epithets at MT 6:9 are 1cs-possessive, addressive in flavour but not address forms. The row's bilateral claim therefore holds on the BACK side only, where the 3fs-to-1cs shift into יָרַ֔דְתִּי (oshb:Song.6.11, byte tier) is real and correctly grounds that edge. What the front edge does carry is weaker and different from what the row asserts: the speaker's 1cs possessive epithets drop out after MT 6:9 and the form turns declarative-to-interrogative. TIER DEFECT (OL, distinct, upheld): the row's own מִי זֹ֥את (oshb:Song.6.10) is byte tier at 1 verse; the three-site count is an accent_stripped/skeleton object (sweep: 3 verses at both tiers - MT 3:6, 6:10, 8:5), and no tier is named, against the tier-disclosure standard that a skeleton-tier cohesion driver meets the byte-grounded bar ONLY with the tier honestly named. LABEL DEFECT (OL, distinct, upheld): 'ascending-question' imports a byte-absent element - the ascending verb is attested in מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ (oshb:Song.3.6, byte tier) and at MT 8:5 (word-bound skeleton sweep of that verb: 2 verses, MT 3:6 and MT 8:5) and is ABSENT from MT 6:10, whose participle is הַנִּשְׁקָפָ֖ה. OL's high severity is sustained rather than reduced: this is a single-verse row whose independent existence rests entirely on the front cut, and tier-3 SAMEKH corroboration cannot carry a boundary whose tier-1 evidence does not survive.
orders.remedy: Strike 'bounded on both sides by a person-form shift' from boundary_rationale. If the row survives the escalated boundary question, state the front-edge signals in their true terms - loss of the speaker's 1cs possessive epithets after MT 6:9, the declarative-to-interrogative form change, and the mi-zot formula anchor - and tier-label that recurrence as accent_stripped/skeleton (sweep: 3 verses), replacing 'ascending-question' with a label MT 6:10's own bytes carry (the participial who-is-this-who-looks-out class). Re-cut observed_substrate_signals to the surviving driver, and re-open rejected_alternative and confidence with it. Cure tests (the tests that killed the original): a word-final-kaf plus 1cs/3fs audit over MT 6:9-6:10 must not contradict any person-shift wording left on the row; every recurrence sentence must name its tier; and no element of a formula label may be asserted that a sweep of the row's own verse cannot find.

orders.challenge_claim: The row never argues its own front boundary: neither the rationale nor boundary_evidence_refs addresses why the row does not continue 6:12's voice, despite an available tier-1 warrant.
orders.grounds: Verified against the row and the bytes. boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative address only the verse's internal two-voice structure and the BACK seam; MT 6:12 appears nowhere on the row, and the refs-mirror check returns GREEN precisely because no out-of-span mention of 6:12 exists to mirror - the silence is total, not a citation slip. The unused tier-1 warrant is real: oshb:Song.6.12 closes in first person singular (לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי, נַפְשִׁ֣י, שָׂמַ֔תְנִי, oshb:Song.6.12, byte tier) and oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13 opens with a repeated 2fs imperative summons שׁ֤וּבִי שׁ֨וּבִי֙ הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית (byte tier) addressed to an epithet unique to this verse (הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית; byte sweep: 1 verse book-wide, 2 occurrences in-verse) - an addressee-and-person shift of exactly the tier-1 class. One collateral assertion in the LF item is itself byte-false and is NOT adopted: the row's offset-zone dual-cite discipline is not followed throughout (see the OL ruling on this row); the front-boundary finding survives that correction.
orders.remedy: Add the front-seam argument to boundary_rationale with both forms spliced and tier-labelled - the 1cs run at oshb:Song.6.12 against the 2fs imperative summons and the הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית epithet at oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13 - and add web:Song.6.12 to boundary_evidence_refs. In the same edit disclose the catchword that crosses this seam: נָדִֽיב (oshb:Song.6.12, byte tier) immediately before and בַּת נָדִ֑יב (oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1, byte tier) immediately after, skeleton sweep: 2 verses book-wide, bracketing the single-verse span on both seams. Cure test: every verse argued in prose outside the row's own span appears in boundary_evidence_refs and the refs-mirror check stays GREEN after the addition; the front seam must be defensible from an in-verse marker, never from the WEB voice heading.

orders.challenge_claim: The row states that every structured ref on it carries the dual-cite qualifier and that is false - its rejected-alternative sentence carries a bare offset-zone coordinate - and it argues its own held voice crux without quoting the verse's decisive plural form.
orders.grounds: Both halves verified, including OL's account of why no machine flag fires - DISTINCT from the LF item on this row, which concerns the unargued front seam. strongest_rejected_alternative writes the structured coordinate 'web:Song.7.1' (i.e. web:Song.7.1 = oshb:Song.7.2) bare on the row - no dual, no numeric qualifier - while device_notes asserts that every structured ref on the row carries the dual-cite qualifier. In this book that bare coordinate resolves to oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1, and standing in a sentence about extending the row FORWARD it is readable as the row's own verse (web:Song.6.13 = oshb:Song.7.1) - the exact ambiguity the offset-zone rule exists to prevent. Machine state confirms the rule-level character of the leak: the citation sweep returns GREEN for these rows because its offset-zone disclosure arm iterates the boundary_evidence_refs list only (confirmed at source), so a bare offset-zone coordinate sitting in a prose field is not covered; the universals check independently flags 'every structured ref on it carries the dual-cite qualifier' as a digit-less universal, and it is false on the row's own text. Engagement gap verified: the row quotes the summons and תֶּחֱזוּ֙ (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier) but omits the form between them - וְנֶחֱזֶה בָּ֑ךְ (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier), a 1cp cohortative with a 2fs suffix - which is the in-verse byte evidence that the summoners are plural and the addressee feminine, exactly the question the row holds open.
orders.remedy: Qualify the coordinate in strongest_rejected_alternative as 'web:Song.7.1 = oshb:Song.7.2' (or 'web:Song.7.1 (MT 7:2)'), and either delete the device_notes universal or restate it as a checked claim. Splice וְנֶחֱזֶה בָּ֑ךְ (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier) into the crux sentence, tier-labelled, as the plural-speaker evidence being weighed against the 2mp תֶּחֱזוּ֙ - the crux stays HELD, not decided. Cure test (the test that killed the original is prose-side, not machine-side): a hand sweep of EVERY structured coordinate in EVERY field, not only boundary_evidence_refs, must show a dual or numeric qualifier on each, since the deterministic arm does not reach prose fields; and no unsupported universal may remain on the row.

orders.challenge_claim: The curly-quoted WEB citation for web:Song.7.1 = oshb:Song.7.2 substitutes a straight apostrophe for the source's curly apostrophe, breaking byte-verbatim fidelity inside an otherwise well-grounded wasf-boundary claim.
orders.grounds: The byte fact is confirmed; the framing and the scope are both wrong. Exact-substring test (no punctuation normalisation) of every curly-quoted WEB span in this cluster's seven rows against the staged WEB verse text: 10 spans tested, exactly 3 fail, all three by U+0027 standing where the source carries U+2019 - web:Song.7.1 = oshb:Song.7.2 (source reads “prince’s daughter!”), web:Song.7.10 = oshb:Song.7.11 (“I am my beloved’s.”) and web:Song.7.11 = oshb:Song.7.12 (“Let’s go out into the field.”); the other seven spans are exact, including both of P02-012's and the long adjuration span at web:Song.8.4. So the defect is real but it is a THREE-SITE CLASS, not the single site the challenge frames. Severity correction: the campaign's WEB-verbatim arm is punctuation-normalised BY DESIGN (it is a gloss-as-WEB detector) and returns GREEN on all seven rows, and the mandatory register rule governs the ENCLOSING curly double quotes plus an inline web: ref in the same field, which every row here satisfies; the straight apostrophes inside the row's own Hebrew glosses are correct under the same rule. Tier: English-witness transcription fidelity - no Hebrew tier, no boundary warrant and no evidence ref moves on this finding.
orders.remedy: One sweep, not three spot fixes: in boundary_rationale of P02-010, P02-013 and P02-014 replace U+0027 with U+2019 inside the curly-quoted WEB spans ONLY, leaving the straight apostrophes in the straight-quoted Hebrew glosses untouched. Test the cure must pass: an exact-substring test with punctuation normalisation DISABLED of every curly-quoted span in the revised rows against the staged WEB verse text - the test that returned 3 failures out of 10 here must return 10 of 10.

orders.challenge_claim: The row states an arithmetically false numbering-space identity for the offset zone and leaves its front seam - the book's crosswalk seam - uncited, while the tier-1 gender marker its own signal key rests on runs unbroken across that cut.
orders.grounds: Defect 1 is the load-bearing one and is confirmed: boundary_rationale reads '(WEB ch 7 = MT 7:2-7:6)'. Re-derived from the crosswalk in both directions - WEB ch 7 holds 13 verses and maps to MT 7:2-7:14 (MT ch 7 holds 14); MT 7:2-7:6 is only this row's own span (= WEB 7:1-7:5). A false chapter-level identity written in the one zone where dual discipline binds hardest, and it is invisible to the machine arms: the structured-ref arithmetic and the prose-pair arm both return GREEN on this row because the falsehood is a CHAPTER-level statement in prose. Defect 2 upheld in part and refined: the front neighbour web:Song.6.13 = oshb:Song.7.1 appears in no evidence ref and in no prose, while the 2fs addressee marker IS continuous across that cut - oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13 carries שׁ֤וּבִי four times (2fs imperative) and וְנֶחֱזֶה בָּ֑ךְ (2fs suffix), byte tier, and the row's own opener oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1 reads מַה יָּפ֧וּ with 2fs פְעָמַ֛יִךְ, so only the suffixed-body-part sub-class begins at MT 7:2 and a tier-1 address marker straddles the front seam undisclosed. REFINED: OL's supporting sub-claim that the praise-exclamation CONSTRUCTION also straddles the cut does not hold at its own digit - the skeleton sweep OL cites (3 verses: MT 4:10, MT 7:2 = WEB 7:1, MT 7:7 = WEB 7:6) is a sweep of the mah-plus-yod-pe opener, an object that EXCLUDES MT 7:1; מַֽה תֶּחֱזוּ֙ at MT 7:1 shares only the bare interrogative particle, which is not that device. Right digit, wrong count-object for the straddle claim. Defect 3 upheld at low: מֶ֖לֶךְ אָס֥וּר at oshb:Song.7.6 = web:Song.7.5 is the anarthrous member of the melek-lexeme set (independently re-swept: 5 verses, MT 1:4, 1:12, 3:9, 3:11, 7:6), and the row's straight-quoted byte-tier gloss 'the king is held captive' imports the English witness's definiteness. Tier-4 audit only, never evidence in either direction: OL's note that the uncited front seam coincides with a WEB [SPEAKER] apparatus site is correctly labelled and correctly excluded from the warrant. Convergence: LF's item on this row is a DISTINCT defect from OL's - no overlap.
orders.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: delete the false parenthetical and state either the span-level relation already carried in boundary_evidence_refs or an arithmetically correct chapter statement (WEB ch 7 = MT 7:2-7:14). Test: re-derive the chapter mapping with the crosswalk in BOTH directions and confirm the 13/14 verse counts before any chapter-level identity is written - the arithmetic that killed the original, and one no validator arm performs on prose, so a GREEN suite re-run does not certify this cure. (2) boundary_evidence_refs: add the front-seam pair web:Song.6.13 = oshb:Song.7.1, and disclose in boundary_rationale that the 2fs addressee marker runs ACROSS the front cut while only the suffixed-body-part run begins at oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1, with spliced byte-tier forms on both sides. Test: the front-seam claim must quote a gender-marked form on both sides of the cut, not on one. (3) Re-cut the MT 7:6 gloss to the anarthrous bytes.

orders.challenge_claim: strongest_rejected_alternative engages only the weaker back-fold rival and omits the stronger, undisclosed forward-fold rival into the second wasf run.
orders.grounds: Confirmed. The row's strongest_rejected_alternative addresses only attachment to the preceding wasf; the forward fold into the second wasf run (web:Song.7.7-Song.7.9 = oshb:Song.7.8-Song.7.10) is engaged nowhere in the row. LF's device object re-derived independently rather than reproduced: the skeleton sweep of the praise-exclamation opener returns exactly 3 verses - MT 4:10, MT 7:2 = WEB 7:1, MT 7:7 = WEB 7:6 - so מַה יָּפִית֙ וּמַה נָּעַ֔מְתְּ in the row's own verse shares its opener formula with the FIRST wasf's opener מַה יָּפ֧וּ (skeleton tier, named as such), which makes 'this verse OPENS a wasf run' the strongest available rival rather than the back-fold the row declined. Aggravating and found independently here: the warrant offered on both sides is that 'the mechanically derived run ends at MT 7:6' - the derived wasf zone is a staging signal and is barred as row evidence, so the one rival the row does engage is refused on a non-evidentiary ground. NEW FINDING (neither primary): boundary_evidence_refs on this one-verse row carries its own verse and the PRECEDING span only - the forward neighbour web:Song.7.7 = oshb:Song.7.8 is absent, so the very seam the challenge concerns is uncited, and the row's seam citation is asymmetric. LF's tier-3 absence citation (no PE and no SAMEKH between MT 6:10 and MT 7:11) re-verified against the parashah inventory and correctly handled - absence is never counterevidence, and LF says so explicitly.
orders.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the back-fold sentence with the forward-fold rival (this verse as the opening exclamation of the wasf run at web:Song.7.7-Song.7.9 = oshb:Song.7.8-Song.7.10), declined on argued bytes; delete the derived-run appeal from the rationale and from the rival sentence alike; boundary_evidence_refs: add web:Song.7.7 = oshb:Song.7.8. Test the replacement warrant must pass - the test that killed the original: it must dispose of the 3-verse skeleton-tier opener formula (MT 4:10, MT 7:2 = WEB 7:1, MT 7:7 = WEB 7:6) on bytes alone, with no appeal to the mechanically derived run and no appeal to a speaker heading.

orders.challenge_claim: The single-verse cut is carried by a voice-shift signal key, but the bytes show no shift at all - same speaker, same 2fs addressee across MT 7:6-7:8 - and the vocative construal that supplies the only other warrant is undecidable on the staged evidence.
orders.grounds: The bytes are exactly as stated and the mislabel is real; the granularity framing over-reaches. CONFIRMED: oshb:Song.7.7 = web:Song.7.6 reads מַה יָּפִית֙ וּמַה נָּעַ֔מְתְּ - both perfects 2fs, carrying no final qamats where the 2ms counterparts would - flanked by 2fs body-part suffixes at oshb:Song.7.6 = web:Song.7.5 (רֹאשֵׁ֤ךְ עָלַ֨יִךְ֙) and oshb:Song.7.8 = web:Song.7.7 (קֽוֹמָתֵךְ֙), byte tier, with both witnesses reading one continuous address. No speaker change and no addressee change sits at either seam, so the observed_substrate_signals key voice_shift.transitional_address_exclamation is byte-false: the field contract requires the key to name the signal class actually consulted, and the class consulted here is a wasf form-class edge. REFINED (framing and severity): the conclusion that the cut is what the granularity rule forbids does not survive its own consequences - read that way the rule would equally forbid the two flanking wasf rows, which sit inside the SAME single voice; the owner's vocabulary makes wasf bounds writer-argued form-class seams (openers, closures, addressee shifts), so a wasf-to-non-wasf edge inside one voice is a licensed boundary. What is curable is the driver LABEL and the missing continuity disclosure, not the existence of the cut. Second defect upheld at low: 'as a vocative' for אַהֲבָ֖ה בַּתַּֽעֲנוּגִֽים is decided rather than held - the noun is anarthrous, no morphology layer is staged, and the rival construal (love as the exclamation's subject) stands on the same bytes, so the vocative reading tracks the English rendering and must be disclosed as held. Independently re-derived and CLEAN: the row's digit claim 'one of the ten ahavah-noun sites (sweep: 10 verses)' - the bare skeleton sweep returns 15 verses, less the 5 she-ahavah relative-verb formula verses (MT 1:7, 3:1-4), leaving 10 noun sites including MT 7:7; object correctly split, digit correct. Convergence: LF's item and OL's are DISTINCT defects at the same seam - a missing rival versus a byte-false driver key - and together they show one underlying weakness, that the isolation rests on a staging signal plus a mislabelled key rather than on bytes.
orders.remedy: observed_substrate_signals: replace the voice_shift.* key with a wasf form-class key (e.g. wasf.form_class_edge_non_body_part), and re-open every field the contract makes dependent on a driver swap - boundary_rationale, strongest_rejected_alternative, unit_type, confidence. boundary_rationale must state that speaker and 2fs addressee are CONTINUOUS across both seams, with spliced byte-tier forms from oshb:Song.7.6 = web:Song.7.5, oshb:Song.7.7 = web:Song.7.6 and oshb:Song.7.8 = web:Song.7.7, and must hold the ahavah vocative construal open instead of asserting it. Test the cure must pass: no voice_shift.* key may stand on this row unless a gender-marked form or an attested formula anchor CHANGES at one of its seams - the test the original key fails.

orders.challenge_claim: The row's own last verse carries her address-word for him, undisclosed, contradicting the row's single-voice attribution and binding that verse forward into the mutual-belonging refrain across the row's back seam.
orders.grounds: Upheld on bytes. oshb:Song.7.10 = web:Song.7.9 - the row's own final verse - reads הוֹלֵ֥ךְ לְדוֹדִ֖י לְמֵישָׁרִ֑ים (byte tier); dodi is her word for him and is a tier-1 address vocabulary under the owner's moderate voice-attribution policy. The row is typed wasf_poem on the single signal key wasf.body_part_run_2fs_suffixes and quotes only that verse's closing three words דּוֹבֵ֖ב שִׂפְתֵ֥י יְשֵׁנִֽים, never the dodi clause. Both witnesses carry it - WEB renders “that goes down smoothly for my beloved” at web:Song.7.9 = oshb:Song.7.10 - so this is not an apparatus artefact. The token then repeats immediately across the back seam as אֲנִ֣י לְדוֹדִ֔י at oshb:Song.7.11 = web:Song.7.10, and the independent skeleton sweep of that exact form returns 5 verses (MT 5:5, 5:6, 6:3, 7:10 = WEB 7:9, 7:11 = WEB 7:10): a byte-true tier-1 device straddling the row's own seam, which argues continuity against the cut unless disclosed. The row's back-seam warrant instead rests on imagery class plus 'matching the mechanically derived wasf boundary exactly', a staging signal barred as row evidence. REFINED sub-claim: the inference that the voice turn therefore sits INSIDE oshb:Song.7.10 = web:Song.7.9 is a construal the staged evidence cannot decide - no morphology layer is staged and both witnesses admit either the man taking up her word or her interjection - so it is held, not adopted. CONVERGENCE, and the decisive one in this cluster: LF SUPPORTED this row, certifying that both WEB quotes are byte-verbatim and that the live forward rival is correctly engaged, and LF's own evidence field quotes the closing run of oshb:Song.7.10 = web:Song.7.9 IN FULL, dodi clause included, without flagging it. The two primaries are not addressing the same defect: LF found none, and LF's support is itself defective. Tier-4 audit only, never evidence: OL's note that the chosen back seam coincides with a WEB [SPEAKER] apparatus site before web:Song.7.10 = oshb:Song.7.11 is correctly labelled non-evidential and is recorded solely as an audit against heading-leaning at the one seam where the row's own Hebrew runs the other way.
orders.remedy: boundary_rationale must disclose the dodi token at oshb:Song.7.10 = web:Song.7.9 with a spliced byte-tier form, state how the unit's voice attribution survives a token of the OTHER address vocabulary standing inside its own span, and disclose the repetition at oshb:Song.7.11 = web:Song.7.10 as cross-seam cohesion; strongest_rejected_alternative must decline the forward extension without the derived-run appeal; device_notes must name the swept object precisely (dodi-exact, not dod-family) wherever a dod digit is used. Test the cure must pass: delete the derived-run sentence and the revised back-seam warrant must still stand, and it must dispose of the 5-verse skeleton-tier chain of that exact form across the seam - the two supports the original never faced.

orders.challenge_claim: LF: an unscoped 'hapax' universal claim lacking the mandated digit-bearing sweep disclosure, plus the apostrophe defect. OL: the row names a Hebrew form that is not in its span - MT 7:13 reads the 1cs defective dodai, not a 2ms 'dodekha' - and its mandrake and cohortative labels are likewise off the bytes.
orders.grounds: Upheld, and the severity rises above both primaries' medium: the lead defect is a Hebrew FORM named in row prose that the cited bytes do not carry, standing in the very row that owns the token, in the book whose signature hazard is dod-family blending. CONFIRMED (the form): oshb:Song.7.13 = web:Song.7.12 reads אֶת דֹּדַ֖י לָֽךְ (byte tier). The attested token is דֹּדַ֖י - 1cs, no second-person suffix in the consonants at all - and both witnesses read the speaker's own possessive (WEB “There I will give you my love.” at web:Song.7.12 = oshb:Song.7.13), whereas device_notes calls it 'the defective-spelling dodekha token', a 2ms form absent from these bytes. Re-swept independently: the defective spelling returns exactly 4 verses (MT 1:2, 1:4, 4:10, 7:13 = WEB 1:2, 1:4, 4:10, 7:12); MT 1:2 and 1:4 carry a 2ms suffix and MT 4:10 the 2fs דֹדַ֖יִךְ, so MT 7:13 is the single member whose suffix runs the other way - wrong form and wrong direction of address in the row that argues who addresses whom. CONVERGENT, the SAME defect from both primaries: 'the mandrakes hapax' carries no scope and no digit. Re-swept: הַֽדּוּדָאִ֣ים returns 1 verse in this book (MT 7:14 = WEB 7:13); the staged evidence supports only a book-scoped digit, and 'hapax' is a universal claim requiring the adjacent digit-bearing citation that names object and unit. The automated universal arm does not carry 'hapax' in its claim vocabulary, so this class is reachable only by review - and both primaries reached it. CONFIRMED (the form labels): 'One sustained 1cs voice' and 'her single cohortative address' mis-state the run - the cohortatives in the span are first-person PLURAL, נֵצֵ֣א and נָלִ֖ינָה at oshb:Song.7.12 = web:Song.7.11 and נַשְׁכִּ֨ימָה֙ and נִרְאֶ֞ה at oshb:Song.7.13 = web:Song.7.12, while the genuinely 1cs forms are אֶתֵּ֥ן and צָפַ֥נְתִּי; the automated universal arm independently flagged the word 'single' in that same sentence. The signal key voice_shift.1cs_cohortative_invitation inherits the error. LF's apostrophe half is confirmed (web:Song.7.11 = oshb:Song.7.12 reads “Let’s go out into the field.”) but belongs to the three-site class cured by one sweep.
orders.remedy: device_notes: name the MT 7:13 token by its attested form - the 1cs defective spelling, spliced, byte tier, dual-cited oshb:Song.7.13 = web:Song.7.12 - and state the direction of address it actually carries; scope the mandrakes claim to the book with its digit ('sweep: 1 verse in this book'). boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative: replace 1cs with 1cp for the cohortative chain and re-key observed_substrate_signals accordingly, re-opening rationale, rejected_alternative, unit_type and confidence as dependents of the driver swap. boundary_evidence_refs: add the back-seam pair web:Song.7.13 = oshb:Song.7.14 | web:Song.8.1, currently uncited on both sides. Test the cure must pass: every Hebrew FORM named in prose must be re-spliced from its cited verse and re-collated at byte tier before the row ships - the check both 'dodekha' and '1cs cohortative' fail - and the mandrakes scope must carry a digit naming object and unit.

orders.challenge_claim: OL: the rival dialogue reading is rejected on a ground the bytes contest, and the book's only two wall-noun sites sit on either side of the row's own back seam, undisclosed. (LF supported this row.)
orders.grounds: The load-bearing half is upheld; the framing half is corrected. UPHELD: חוֹמָ֣ה (oshb:Song.8.9) and חוֹמָ֔ה (oshb:Song.8.10) are the lexeme's only two sites in the book (skeleton sweep: 2 verses), they are adjacent, and they are identical only once cantillation is stripped (byte tier at each ref, accent_stripped tier as a pair). The answer is clause-for-clause: אִם חוֹמָ֣ה הִ֔יא is answered by אֲנִ֣י חוֹמָ֔ה, and וְשָׁדַ֖יִם אֵ֣ין לָ֑הּ is answered by וְשָׁדַ֖י כַּמִּגְדָּל֑וֹת (byte tier at their own refs). That byte-true device straddles the row's own back seam with nothing in the prose disclosing it, while web:Song.8.10-Song.8.12 sits in boundary_evidence_refs without ever being argued. REFINED: the challenge says the bytes contest the stated ground; they do not. 'One speaker-group without an answering party' is byte-true of the span's interior - oshb:Song.8.8 carries לָ֨נוּ֙, נַּעֲשֶׂה֙, לַאֲחֹתֵ֔נוּ and oshb:Song.8.9 carries נִבְנֶ֥ה and נָצ֥וּר, all 1cp, all byte tier. The corrected finding is that the rejected alternative engages the wrong rival: the live rival the bytes make available is a Song.8.8-Song.8.10 dialogue_exchange, not a Song.8.8-Song.8.9 one, and the row never reaches it. LF's support of this row is independently verified and not contradicted (see supported_sample): the 1cp front seam and the achot role-split are both sound, and the back seam survives the straddling device because the 1cp-to-1cs person change at oshb:Song.8.9|8.10 is in-verse and marked.
orders.remedy: Disclose the straddling wall-noun and breast answer at the Song.8.9|8.10 seam in boundary_rationale, splicing both sides at byte tier and naming the tiers honestly (byte at each ref; identical only at accent_stripped tier as a pair), and state why the seam survives it - the marked 1cp-to-1cs person change. Replace the rejected alternative's rival with a Song.8.8-Song.8.10 dialogue_exchange, within the one-sentence limit. Either argue web:Song.8.10-Song.8.12 in prose or drop the ref. NEW (neither packet): the identification of the speaker-group AS the brothers is carried by content inference alone - no in-verse form names them - while the byte anchor that would carry it sits unused at oshb:Song.1.6, בְּנֵ֧י אִמִּ֣י (byte tier), the same verse that supplies the keeper-and-vineyard chain linking oshb:Song.1.6, oshb:Song.8.11 and oshb:Song.8.12 (skeleton sweep: 3 verses); cite it or lower the attribution's stated tier. TESTS the cure must pass: (1) no byte-true device straddles the row's seam undisclosed; (2) the rejected alternative names the strongest rival the bytes make available; (3) every attribution states the tier that carries it.

orders.challenge_claim: OL: the quoted marker is a common-gender pronoun and cannot carry the row's return to her own voice, the verse's actual gender-bearing forms go unquoted, and the petuchah is placed inside the verse rather than at the division it closes. (LF supported this row, calling the pronoun an unambiguous tier-1 marker and the mark correctly disclosed.)
orders.grounds: Upheld on both counts, and LF's support is refuted in part. אֲנִ֣י (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier) fixes person and number only; set against the 1cp נִבְנֶ֥ה and נָצ֥וּר of oshb:Song.8.9 (byte tier) it is genuine tier-1 evidence for a SPEAKER change, so the seam itself stands and LF is right that far - but the owner voice policy requires the gender-marked form to be quoted for the attribution, and this verse's gender-bearing forms sit unquoted inside it: כְּמוֹצְאֵ֥ת, a feminine-singular participle, בְעֵינָ֖יו, a 3ms suffix locating the other party as a man, and וְשָׁדַ֖י כַּמִּגְדָּל֑וֹת answering oshb:Song.8.8 (all byte tier). Second count, also upheld: the mark inventory is verse-keyed and this cluster's own rows read a seg as closing its verse - the setumah at MT 8:4 is cited as the front seam of Song.8.5, the setumah at MT 8:7 as the front seam of Song.8.8 - so the book's single petuchah at MT 8:10 corroborates the MT 8:10|8:11 division, which is this row's BACK seam, not the front seam the row attaches it to; and 'sitting exactly at this pronoun-marked return' is an intra-verse position claim a verse-keyed single-witness inventory cannot source. The 1-of-20 digit, the petuchah-versus-setumah distinction and the single-witness disclosure are correct, and the mark is not treated as the driver.
orders.remedy: Splice כְּמוֹצְאֵ֥ת שָׁלֽוֹם and בְעֵינָ֖יו (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier) into the seam warrant so the attribution rests on a gender-marked form, keeping אֲנִ֣י as the person-and-number marker it actually is. Re-cut the parashah sentence to the division the seg closes (MT 8:10|8:11) and delete the intra-verse placement; the dependent signal key must move from a self-marker to a back-seam key, since the driver framing changed. Re-open confidence, which was set above its siblings on the strength of the marker now corrected. TESTS the cure must pass: (1) the row's voice-attribution claim quotes a gender-marked form at byte tier; (2) no parashah citation asserts an intra-verse position or is attached to a seam the seg does not touch; (3) the confidence band is re-derived after the driver change rather than carried over.

orders.challenge_claim: LF: boundary_rationale and boundary_evidence_refs name only the tier-3 petuchah at MT 8:10 as the stated front-seam evidence; the actual tier-1 warrant, the person shift from her 1cs declaration into 3ms narration naming Solomon, is disclosed only inside strongest_rejected_alternative.
orders.grounds: Upheld, and DISTINCT from OL's item on this same row - LF's is a tier-discipline placement defect, OL's is a false person claim; they are not the same defect and both stand. The rationale's one explicit seam citation is the preceding verse's petuchah, tier-3 corroboration that may never be a driver, while the grammatical pivot is real and left out of the field where warrant is expected: אֲנִ֣י חוֹמָ֔ה (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier) gives way to third-person narration כֶּ֣רֶם הָיָ֤ה לִשְׁלֹמֹה֙ with 3ms נָתַ֥ן and בְּפִרְי֖וֹ (oshb:Song.8.11, byte tier). Unlike P02-020, the mark is correctly PLACED here - a seg closing MT 8:10 does corroborate the MT 8:10|8:11 division - so the defect is that a tier-3 corroborator stands alone in the seam-warrant field, not that it is misapplied.
orders.remedy: Move the person-shift warrant into boundary_rationale with byte-tier splices from oshb:Song.8.10 and oshb:Song.8.11, and demote the petuchah sentence to explicit corroboration (single-witness, tier-3, never the driver), freeing strongest_rejected_alternative for the rival within its one-sentence limit. NEW (neither packet): the same sentence appeals to the strategy's own vineyard-mashal category - a strategy-file citation barred from row prose by the register rule - so the replacement warrant must be argued from bytes, not from a category name. TEST the cure must pass: strike the tier-3 sentence and boundary_rationale must still carry a tier-1 seam warrant on its own bytes.

orders.challenge_claim: OL: the claim that a 1cs possessive marks her voice throughout is false for MT 8:11, which carries no first-person form at all, and the 1cs forms in MT 8:12 are common-gender - the female attribution rests on cross-verse continuity alone.
orders.grounds: Upheld; distinct from LF's item on this row. Re-derived: oshb:Song.8.11 carries no first-person form whatever - its finite verbs are הָיָ֤ה, נָתַ֥ן and יָבִ֥א, and its only person-marked suffix is 3ms בְּפִרְי֖וֹ (byte tier) - so 'throughout' overreaches by exactly the verse the row opens on. At oshb:Song.8.12 the run כָּרְמִ֥י שֶׁלִּ֖י לְפָנָ֑י is common-gender 1cs, and the verse's only person-marked address is 2ms לְךָ֙ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה (byte tier), which the possessive characterization drops entirely. Under the owner voice policy that leaves the female attribution resting on tier-2 cross-verse continuity, barred as a sole driver. OL's proposed byte anchor checks out and is better than the row's: the possessive phrase recurs at oshb:Song.1.6 as כַּרְמִ֥י שֶׁלִּ֖י - the phrase's only two sites (skeleton sweep: 2 verses) - matching at SKELETON tier only, since the first vowel differs, while oshb:Song.1.6 is unambiguously her voice (שֶׁאֲנִ֣י שְׁחַרְחֹ֔רֶת, נֹטֵרָ֣ה, byte tier), and the keeper lexeme links oshb:Song.1.6, oshb:Song.8.11 and oshb:Song.8.12 (skeleton sweep: 3 verses).
orders.remedy: Rewrite the attribution: drop 'throughout', restrict the 1cs possessive claim to oshb:Song.8.12, and add לְךָ֙ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה as part of what that verse attests. Carry the female attribution on the oshb:Song.1.6 anchor, cited at SKELETON tier for the phrase pair - byte tier is unavailable there, the first vowel differs - together with the byte-tier feminine forms at oshb:Song.1.6, and add oshb:Song.1.6 to boundary_evidence_refs with the cross-row reference verse-anchored. TESTS the cure must pass: (1) no person or gender claim is asserted over a verse that does not attest the form; (2) every recurrence claim names the tier that carries it, and a skeleton-tier match is never written as verbatim; (3) the mirrored ref set covers every verse argued outside the row's own span.

orders.challenge_claim: LF: the Hebrew quote excludes 'chaverim' yet the attached gloss translates it - a quote/gloss same-span violation. OL: the same parity defect, plus the row's warrant that gender marking is thin across both verses, which the bytes contest with the span's cleanest 2fs/2ms minimal pair and the policy's first-named tier-1 address word.
orders.grounds: Two findings on one row: the parity defect is the SAME defect in both packets; OL's marker-thinness finding is DISTINCT and additional; both upheld. Parity: MT 8:13 reads חֲבֵרִ֛ים immediately before the row's run מַקְשִׁיבִ֥ים לְקוֹלֵ֖ךְ הַשְׁמִיעִֽינִי (re-collated: byte tier at oshb:Song.8.13), and 'companions' stands unbracketed in the gloss; the run is additionally mislabelled a 2fs imperative summons, since its first word מַקְשִׁיבִ֥ים is a masculine-plural participle agreeing with those companions - only הַשְׁמִיעִֽינִי is the feminine-singular imperative. Marker thinness: read off the pointed codepoints, לְקוֹלֵ֖ךְ (oshb:Song.8.13) ends final kaf plus sheva, the 2fs shape, and לְךָ֤ (oshb:Song.8.14) ends final kaf plus qamats, the 2ms shape - a byte-level minimal pair across the row's internal seam - alongside הַיוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת standing in vocative position, the masculine-singular imperatives בְּרַ֣ח and וּֽדְמֵה, and the explicit vocative דּוֹדִ֗י, the address word the owner voice policy names first. The digit for that address vocabulary is 24 verses in its attested exact spellings, and the object matters: a contiguous-consonant sweep returns 25 because it also catches דּוֹדִֽים at oshb:Song.5.1, which is the lovers-noun, not her address word - the five-object dod trap, avoided here. So the row's stated warrant, that the markers are too thin to argue a tier-1 seam, is contradicted by its own two verses; holding the pair as one dialogue_exchange stays defensible on the hold-whole ground, but on a different warrant and a re-derived confidence band. Tier-4: no WEB speaker heading is relied on by either packet or by this ruling, in either direction.
orders.remedy: Re-cut the gloss to its run, or extend the run to include חֲבֵרִ֛ים and re-collate to byte tier, and drop the 2fs-imperative label from the masculine-plural participle. Replace the thin-markers warrant with the hold-whole warrant, quoting the לְקוֹלֵ֖ךְ against לְךָ֤ pair and דּוֹדִ֗י at byte tier and naming the address-vocabulary digit with its object (exact attested spellings, sweep: 24 verses). Re-open confidence, which was pinned to the misstatement. NEW (neither packet): the rejected alternative states that the strategy names this pair as one dialogue_exchange zone - a strategy-file citation barred from row prose by the register rule; re-argue the hold-whole ground from the verses themselves. TESTS the cure must pass: (1) every gloss translates only what its run contains; (2) each speaker turn names the verse it is marked in with the gender-marked form spliced at byte tier; (3) no digit is cited without naming the object swept.

orders.challenge_claim: Both of the row's seams carry undisclosed byte-true straddles - the man's address vocabulary continues into MT 5:2 and the daughters quote the oath back at MT 5:9 - while the opening voice claim is carried by the English rather than by the gender-marked Hebrew.
orders.grounds: All three limbs verify on re-derived bytes. Front seam: פִּתְחִי לִ֞י אֲחֹתִ֤י רַעְיָתִי֙ (byte, oshb:Song.5.2) continues the man's address vocabulary across the seam - the bride-epithet chain of MT 4:9, 4:10, 4:12 and 5:1 (5 verses, word-bound) plus his-word-for-her (9 verses book-wide) - and the qol-dodi opener stands in the same verse (2 sites book-wide). The role split that resolves it is available in both witnesses and is neither performed nor disclosed: the rendering marks the address as embedded direct speech inside her narration (“It is the voice of my beloved who knocks” introducing the quoted call at web:Song.5.2), which is what distinguishes continued address from quoted address - exactly the same speech-role discipline this row already applies elsewhere. Opening voice: the form that actually marks it, אֲנִ֥י יְשֵׁנָ֖ה (byte, oshb:Song.5.2, feminine singular), is never quoted, and the claim rests on “I was asleep, but my heart was awake.” (web:Song.5.2), which carries no gender at all, plus a tier-3 setumah at MT 5:1 - so a tier-1 marker present in the row's own opening verse goes unused while the seam is argued below its available tier. Back seam: שֶׁכָּ֖כָה (byte, oshb:Song.5.9) repeats the oath root immediately across the row's own closing seam, the daughters quoting it back - undisclosed, and it is precisely the same-root site the four-site adjuration count excludes on speech-role grounds (oath root: 5 verses; adjuration sites: 4), so the row's own shape discipline owed the disclosure. That discipline is otherwise exact and no boundary change is proposed: both adjuration quotes collate byte at oshb:Song.5.8 and the shape is correctly held apart from the full daughters-plus-gazelles form and from the third variant, with no harmonized shape anywhere, and the rival of isolating the refrain verse is explicitly disclosed - the one refrain-verse decision in this cluster that discharges that duty.
orders.remedy: Two fields, one row (P02-002). (1) boundary_rationale: quote the feminine-marked opening form at oshb:Song.5.2, spliced and tier-labeled byte, as the ground for the opening voice, keeping the rendering as corroboration only. (2) device_notes: disclose both straddles and perform the speech-role split - the address vocabulary continuing into MT 5:2 stands INSIDE the man's quoted call framed by her narration, not as continued address across the seam; and the oath root recurring at MT 5:9 is the daughters quoting it back, the same-root site the four-site count excludes on speech-role grounds. TESTS THE CURE MUST PASS: every voice-shift seam claim quotes the gender-marked Hebrew form, spliced and tier-labeled, and a genderless rendering cannot carry it; no byte-true device may straddle either of the row's seams undisclosed; and the speech-role split must be stated in the same terms the row already uses to keep the adjuration site count at four.
